\paragraph{Why minimum intervention works.}
Restraint in downweighting outperforms aggressiveness.
In the 38.2\% of batches where $\aeff$ determines $\bstar$, the selected exponent is 4.9$\times$ lower than the ESS-only upper bound (\S\ref{sec:regime}), preventing unnecessary suppression of borderline samples ($q \approx 0.4$--$0.6$); this rate is robust across contamination levels (33.4\% at $\rho{=}0.6$) and seeds (CV ${<}2\%$).
The aggregate mean $\bstar \approx 1.4$ as a fixed exponent yields PPL no better than uniform (17.693 vs.\ 17.694), confirming that per-batch adaptation is essential.

\paragraph{Failure modes.}
The method degrades at $\rho{=}0.2$ ($+$0.046 PPL): the detector's mean $q$-score (0.393) indicates poor discrimination, yet $\aeff$-binding occurs in ${\sim}$60\% of batches, causing active but misdirected reweighting that suppresses useful data (Appendix~\ref{app:rho02}).
Both generative detectors fail via the same mechanism: GPT-2 PPL (AUC\,=\,0.91, $\Delta{=}{+}0.10$) and N-gram PPL (AUC\,=\,0.73, $\Delta{=}{+}0.13$) assign high $q$-scores to fluent human text, conflating predictability with synthetic origin.
AUC alone does not determine effectiveness; discriminative signal (TF-IDF+LR, AUC\,=\,0.94, ECE\,=\,0.048) targeting provenance markers is necessary.

\paragraph{Soft vs.\ hard filtering.}
The 3-seed epoch-matched experiment (\S\ref{sec:main-results}) resolves the apparent D\&R advantage: at equal content epochs, D\&R ($17.657 \pm 0.006$) and adaptive $\bstar$ ($17.651 \pm 0.007$) are equivalent ($\Delta{=}0.006$).
D\&R's best full-length PPL (17.250 at $q{>}0.3$) requires ${\sim}$3.2$\times$ effective training compute and a calibrated threshold: the raw U-shaped curve is entirely a multi-epoch artifact (Figure~\ref{fig:dr_dual_curve}).
Soft reweighting sidesteps this: no threshold, no data discarded, and parity at equal epochs suggests provenance-based weighting substitutes for hard filtration without information loss.
A hybrid approach (hard removal at $q{>}0.95$ + adaptive, PPL\,=\,17.514) further improves but assigns $w{=}0$, conflicting with minimum intervention; its advantage likely also stems from multi-epoch exposure.

\paragraph{$\tau$ and deployment.}
$\tau \in [0.5, 0.8]$ all outperform uniform (Table~\ref{tab:tau}); sensitivity is asymmetric (over-cleaning degrades sharply, under-cleaning is mild), and $\tau \in [0.7, 0.8]$ is robust across $\rho \in \{0.4, 0.6\}$ (Appendix~\ref{app:tau_rho}).
$\tau$ remains an empirical hyperparameter; its theoretical derivation is an open problem (\S\ref{sec:limitations}).
For deployment, the method requires a discriminative detector with AUC ${\geq}$ 0.94; $\tau{=}0.8$ and $\nmin{=}\lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ serve as defaults.
Pareto-smoothed importance sampling diagnostics~\citep{vehtari2024psis} could provide per-batch weight reliability estimates; we leave this to future work.
